source_review.notes: Checked current official Amazon S3 multipart overview, completion, checksum, abort, and limits documentation; Google Cloud Storage resumable, XML multipart, and compose documentation; and Azure Put Block and Put Block List documentation. Sources support session identity, part replacement/order, checksum/validator handling, completion visibility, ambiguous/in-flight abort behavior, limits, resumability, block-list commit, and cleanup claims. All ten URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed source length, nominal part size, ceiling part count, ordered intervals, session, authoritative/server versus client records, completion manifest, concurrency, wave count, and byte accounting.
Checked part number, byte offset, validator, checksum, full digest, destination version, and application operation identity remain separate.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Provider-specific numbering, offset, block-ID, and resumable-session models are not conflated.

evidence: Executed multipart-commit-accounting with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 25-GiB size, 128-MiB part size, 200 parts, 25 waves, and 1-GiB modeled payload buffer.
Reproduced selected part lengths three, two, and three; committed AAAB2CCC bytes; length eight; SHA-256 prefix 8c7632a93f639477; and unselected part presence.
Recomputed exercise one minimum as about 471.86 MiB, 512-MiB choice as 9,216 parts, 768 ideal waves at concurrency 12, and six-GiB full-part buffer demand.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Payload buffers exclude SDK, protocol, socket, encryption/checksum, retry, and queue memory.

evidence: Derived part count and wave count by ceiling division and modeled payload residency as concurrency times part size.
Checked ordered half-open part intervals cover exactly [0,L) without gap/overlap and completion concatenates only selected manifest parts.
Reviewed attempted, unique selected, and retransmitted byte identities while noting abandoned and protocol terms.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Parallel completion order never substitutes for declared logical byte order.

evidence: Reviewed zero/small/exact/partial/max-count parts, variable sizes, out-of-order completion, duplicate and changed-body part retry, stable/changed sources, and full/composite checksums.

Reviewed crash around remote acceptance/local persistence, pagination with in-flight parts, session expiry, ambiguous completion, concurrent destination writer, abort with active workers, late part success, and cleanup lag.
Reviewed leaked capability URIs, browser origins, key revocation, encryption nonce reuse, retention, sensitive candidates, and regulated research uploads.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Session candidate state, final object state, and downstream dataset publication are separately analyzed.

evidence: Traced stable source identity, exact part position/bytes, returned validators, durable client journal, authoritative reconciliation, ordered completion, destination precondition, and final version verification.
Checked changed bytes cannot silently reuse part identity and completion retry cannot overwrite a later destination version.
Checked abort/cleanup never serves as rollback of an already committed object.
invariant_checking.notes: Worker success count and uploaded byte count do not prove final object creation or correctness.

evidence: Reviewed all ten multipart audit obligations from API selection and initiation through sizing, part integrity, reconciliation, completion, ambiguity, abort, and lifecycle cleanup.

Checked counterexamples for filename-equals-source-version, worker-success-equals-object, completion-order-equals-byte-order, part-ETag-equals-hash, task-count-equals-memory-bound, local-progress-equals-authority, initiation-check-equals-commit-precondition, timeout-equals-no-object, and abort-equals-rollback claims.
Reviewed source snapshot, part coverage, manifest commit, conflict, lost response, in-flight abort, and candidate garbage-collection proof boundaries.
proof_review.notes: Transfer correctness, object atomicity, durability, security, cleanup, and governance require different evidence.

evidence: Audited uses of atomic, exact, stable, successful, authoritative, complete, committed, safe, verified, and durable.
Confirmed the fixture is labeled as abstract numbered-part and resource accounting rather than a provider protocol or cryptographic proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Provider-specific current behavior is scoped to dated official documentation.

evidence: Reviewed retrieval dates, part/request limits, throughput and throttling, retry bytes, buffer residency, session age, candidate bytes, completion ambiguity, cleanup lag, and final verification.
Confirmed no universal optimal part size/concurrency, provider durability, cleanup timing, regulatory approval, certification, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production claims require exact API/provider/library version, source behavior, network, client memory, destination policy, security, and observed cleanup evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed upload families, session intent, stable source, part sizing/identity/integrity, parallelism, durable manifests, resume, completion, visibility, ambiguity, abort, cleanup, preconditions, encryption, observability, and testing as one commit protocol.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed provider limits, session capability protection, byte semaphores, immutable source snapshots, part journals, server reconciliation, destination match conditions, final digest checks, in-flight abort, lifecycle expiration, cost, and browser delegation. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from protocol/state vocabulary through concurrency, recovery, commit, cleanup, and governance; ten examples and five complete answers cover sizing, durable restart, conditional completion, ambiguous expiry, and sensitive delegated upload.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external object-storage protocol expert, cloud-provider representative, transfer-library maintainer, security auditor, research-ethics authority, records specialist, or certification review is claimed.
